proposal.name: cloud_shape
proposal.question: Which of these was it most like?

values.label: a big puffy heap or tower, bulging and rounded on top
a few small separate puffs with soft rounded tops, sky between them
one layer broken into many repeated lumps, rolls or ripples
one smooth almond or lens, clean-edged all round
one long horizontal tube or bar, much longer than it is deep
a smooth featureless sheet, veil or slab with no lumps
thin streaks or brush strokes, like combed hair
torn shreds with frayed edges and no rounded top

proposal.rationale: Same eight-way split as the current question, but the two options people most often swap (tufts and shreds) are now told apart by a stated test: rounded tops versus frayed edges.

why: 2 values for a person to settle

proposal.name: turret_outline
proposal.question: Look at the cloud's upper edge against the sky. Which fits it best?

values.label: a smooth even edge - a flat sheet, or one clean curve like a lens or a bar
gentle rounded bumps, each wider than it is tall
small towers standing up from a shared base, each taller than it is wide, like battlements on a castle wall
one big dome or cauliflower head, much bigger than any bump beside it
ragged, wispy or frayed - no definite edge at all

proposal.rationale: Never uses the word "turret", which the audience does not know; instead it contrasts towers taller-than-wide with bumps wider-than-tall and gives the castle-battlement picture, and it spreads all 32 entries rather than leaving 27 on "no".

why: 5 values for a person to settle

proposal.name: towers_above_layer
proposal.question: Did parts of it stick up well above the rest, like chimneys or towers on a flat roof?

values.label: yes - some parts rose clearly above the general level
no - nothing stood out above the rest

proposal.rationale: A second, independently worded route to the one feature that defines all four castellanus entries, so the quiz can cross-check it instead of betting a whole identification on a single noisy answer.

why: 4 values for a person to settle

proposal.name: streak_detail
proposal.question: If it was made of fine threads or streaks, what were they like?

values.label: it was not made of threads or streaks at all
long threads, about the same thickness the whole way along
threads with a hook or a blob at one end, like a comma, a fishhook or a question mark
small puffs with wisps trailing away below or behind them

proposal.rationale: The current hooks question leaves 30 entries on "no" and is the noisiest in the set; this version gives three everyday pictures of the hook and, in the same breath, separates plain filaments from tufts-with-tails, so it also splits the floccus pairs.

why: 4 values for a person to settle

proposal.name: lump_vs_moon
proposal.question: If it was made of many repeated lumps, grains or rolls, how big did ONE of them look next to the full moon in the sky?

values.label: it was not made of repeated lumps at all
about the moon's size or smaller - little grains, like rice or sand
a few moons wide - small puffs or rolls
far bigger than the moon - big rolls or slabs

proposal.rationale: Apparent element size is the one cue that sorts cirrocumulus from altocumulus from stratocumulus, but finger-widths at arm's length measured 0.27 noise; the moon is a reference everybody has actually looked at, and the three bands match the accepted one-degree and five-degree thresholds.

why: 8 values for a person to settle

proposal.name: lump_shading
proposal.question: Could you see any grey shadow on the lumps?

values.label: there were no lumps to look at
no - every lump was the same bright white all over
yes - each lump was bright on top and clearly darker underneath

proposal.rationale: The current yes/no forces an answer even when there are no lumps, which is probably a large part of its 0.29 noise; adding the explicit "no lumps" escape and describing the cue as bright-on-top-dark-underneath should make the remaining choice a real one.

why: 8 values for a person to settle

proposal.name: shadows_cast
proposal.question: Look at the ground, not the sky: were things casting shadows?

values.label: yes - people, poles or buildings cast a shadow you could see
no - nothing cast any shadow at all

proposal.rationale: Whether a shadow falls is a yes/no an untrained person cannot really get wrong, needs no instrument, and is the classic field test that separates a thin high veil (shadows still cast) from a thick middle or low overcast (none).

why: 3 values for a person to settle

proposal.name: cloud_low_enough
proposal.question: Was it low enough to hide the top of a hill, a tall building or a mast - or to leave the air round you misty?

values.label: yes - it was down among the hilltops or rooftops, or the air was misty
no - it was well clear above everything on the ground

proposal.rationale: The two biggest mix-ups both pit a grey middle-level sheet against stratus, which is simply fog that has not landed; a hilltop or rooftop is a reference in front of the observer, needing no judgement of height in the abstract.

why: 1 values for a person to settle

proposal.name: see_through
proposal.question: Was the cloud itself thin enough to see through - filmy and semi-transparent - or solid?

values.label: thin and filmy - whitish and see-through, blue or the sun's glow came through the cloud itself
solid - it blocked out whatever was behind it

proposal.rationale: A single two-way judgement about the cloud's substance splits the thin ice clouds from the water clouds and separates a dozen listed mix-ups at once, including the high-versus-middle floccus and stratiformis pairs that now rest only on size and shading.

why: 4 values for a person to settle

proposal.name: single_cloud_outline
proposal.question: If it was one cloud on its own, what shape was its outline?

values.label: it was not one cloud - a layer, patch or field of many
one long tube or bar lying across the sky, several times longer than it was deep
one smooth almond or lens, about twice as long as it was deep
one rounded heap or tower, bulging on top
one torn shred with frayed edges

proposal.rationale: The lens-versus-tube confusions are decided by one proportion the eye judges well - how much longer than deep the cloud is - and asking it separately from the eight-way shape question keeps that judgement from being swamped.

why: 1 values for a person to settle

proposal.name: lump_arrangement
proposal.question: How were the lumps laid out?

values.label: lined up in rows, waves or ripples, fairly evenly spaced
scattered about at random, unevenly spaced, with open sky between them
no repeated lumps - one single mass, sheet or shape

proposal.rationale: Regular patterning is what makes a stratiformis or castellanus a layer and a floccus a scatter of separate tufts; pattern-versus-scatter is a glance judgement and does not depend on estimating any size.

why: 2 values for a person to settle

proposal.name: base_look
proposal.question: What was its underside like?

values.label: a definite bottom, flat and level like a ceiling, all at one height
a definite bottom, but bulging downwards in rounded lumps
a torn bottom with wisps and shreds hanging off it
no bottom - it simply thinned away into the sky
you were underneath it and could make out no bottom at all, just even grey

proposal.rationale: The old "flat" and "ragged" options had no middle ground for the rounded, bulging undersides of altocumulus and stratocumulus rolls, so those answers had nowhere sensible to go; splitting flat from lumpy also gives the middle-level layers a cue of their own.

why: 9 values for a person to settle

proposal.name: halo_ring
proposal.question: Was there a complete ring of light right round the sun or moon, standing off from it about the width of your outstretched hand?

values.label: yes - a thin ring or hoop of light, clear of the sun or moon itself
no - at most a bright glare close around it, no ring standing off

proposal.rationale: Most wrong "yes" answers come from people counting the bright glare hugging the sun as a halo; naming the gap, at a hand's width, gives them a test they can apply in a second.
